result:
task: Build W2-92's record route and code route for plain-question `gov retrieve`, wired into `retrieve.py`'s route list, with builder tests and one real-case check.
status: PACKAGES — both routes are built and committed (`46f40ded18a8`), but `gov accept` fails 9 of 30 tests; I think most of the failures come from one conflict in the spec, which needs a decision (P1).
work_completed: (1) `graph_route.start_ids` turns ids in a question into closure start ids. It takes every hyphen-joined run in the question, so ids like `CP-DAEO-0i6h-0001` and `W2-49-CIT-E` are found too. A W2 id is resolved to its ticket through the ticket file's `wbs_id`/`external-ref` field. A register title also counts when the whole title appears in the question, word-bounded and in any case. Only ids and titles the store holds become start ids. `retrieve.py` adds these ids to the existing closure route; when no `--ticket` or `--id` is given, the closure depth is that of radius ≤1. (2) `code_route.route` asks the code index with the tool's own traversal: `search_graph` by name, then `trace_path` one hop each way with cursor paging, then `search_graph` by qualified name in groups of 20. Pages are 50 rows; `query_graph` is never used. Test files are left out, as `trace_path` does by default. Spans are mapped back to repository paths and then to the lexical chunks that cover them, under a new route and facet called `code`. (3) Fail closed: a missing index or one that does not answer makes the `code` facet unavailable, with the reason. That happens only for a question with a word shaped as code (an underscore, camelCase, `name(` or backticks); the other routes still answer. (4) A question that names no record and no symbol adds no facet, route, gap or stopping reason. The budget, batches, continuation, DEC-424's records ahead and W2-87's authority order are untouched.

tests: Existing tests in tests/unit/retrieve, tests/unit/retrieval and tests/unit/closure plus mine: 125 passed, 1 skipped. The skip predates this work (`govbridge` cannot be imported in test_lexical). Mine on their own: 18 passed. `gov accept DAEO-n0wb` (run once): 21 passed, 9 failed. By line: success-1 7/2 (passed/failed); success-2 3/4; success-3 2/4; success-4 9/0; failure-1 9/0; failure-2 1/1; failure-3 2/4. The runner gives counts only, no failure messages, so I could not see why each test failed.
discoveries: (a) W2-13's test_retrieve fixture has no code index and expects a plain question to stop with SATURATED. If a missing index were reported for every question, as the strict reading of KPI 3 asks, that test would break, and so would KPI 4. (b) The code index holds test-support code, including names under tests/acceptance/W2-92/; leaving test files out also keeps that folder out of bundles. (c) `search_graph`'s `name_pattern` ignores case, so the route keeps only exact-case Function, Method or Class rows. (d) Evidence from register chunks carries the register's last entry as its id (`DEC-993`), even when the span is DEC-957's. That comes from existing `record_of` code I did not touch.
risks: (1) Every word of a question is matched against symbol names, so common verbs that are also function names join the code route: "decide" pulled in chunks of `src/gov/guard/decide.py`, and "chunks" matched too. That could hurt hit@5. (2) A caller spanning many lines floods the bundle: `retrieve()` filled 9 of 13 items. (3) Asking the index adds about 6 s to every question while an index exists, mostly the tool's daemon starting. (4) A missing or unreadable index stays silent for a symbol written as a plain word, such as `rrf`; this is the likely cause of the success-3 and failure-3 failures. (5) The tests' stand-in index may not be reachable through the `codeintel._Session` calls I make, which would explain the success-2 and failure-2 failures.
lessons: Edit `retrieve.py` and the store goes stale, so a real-case check after the edit needs either the lead's rebuild or a freshness override. `gov accept` gives no failure messages, so the lead will need them from the runner to diagnose the 9 failures. A question for the lexical route has to be the exact string on a line.
proposed_decisions: P1 — What a missing or unreadable index means for a question whose words are plain. Why now: KPI 3 ("never silently ok") conflicts with KPI 4 and W2-13's no-index test, and it likely explains 8 of the 9 failures. Options, costed as DEC-105 asks: (a) apply now: name the unavailable index for any question with a word; about 2 lines here, but W2-13's test_retrieve needs a change to its expected stopping reason, outside my paths; fully reversible. (b) Defer: keep my rule (only words shaped as code); no cost now, but KPI 3 stays failing. (c) Re-baseline: KPI 3 reads "for a question that names a symbol by its form or as the index knows it". My recommendation is (a) with W2-13's test updated, plus the owner's word on index-less projects, since every question in them would then stop with FACET_UNAVAILABLE. Confidence: medium. P2 — STORE_MISSING (the scope question in my brief). In `retrieve.py`, catch `GovError` with code STORE_MISSING from `_graph`; then use empty `record_of`, `not_current`, `record_types`, `known` and `edges`, skip `register_entries_of` and `order`, leave out the closure and record routes, and set `facets["closure"] = {"available": False, "reason": "the record store is missing or unreadable: …"}`, so the lexical, semantic and code routes still answer. About 12 lines, but in the ranking and setup block, outside the route list. Recommendation: apply it through W2-87's or W2-32's owner. Confidence: medium. P3 — Noise in the code route: a plain word joins only when it follows a code cue (calls, callers of, defined, function or class), or when it is the only match. Judge it with W2-61h's graph and code questions before deciding. About 10 lines; reversible. Confidence: low until measured.
